notes: Built from the 1492 map, adjusted to 1453.
Bosnia (1463), Serbia (1459), the Morea (1460) and Trebizond (1461) were not yet Ottoman.
Skanderbeg's League of Lezhë held northern Albania.
Karaman and Candar (Isfendiyarids) were independent beyliks.
Crimea was independent; it became an Ottoman vassal in 1475.
The Nasrid Emirate of Granada survived until 1492.
Novgorod (1478), Tver (1485) and other Russian lands were not yet Muscovite.
Added the Burgundian State of Philip the Good.
The Teutonic Order still held all of Prussia (until 1466).
Iran and Iraq were ruled by the Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep).
The Deccan was still the united Bahmani Sultanate.
Songhai was a small kingdom around Gao; Mali still held the inner Niger.
The Inca state under Pachacuti covered only the southern Peruvian highlands.
The Triple Alliance under Moctezuma I held only the Valley of Mexico and its surroundings.
In 1453 Mongolia was dominated by the Oirats under Esen Taishi.
The eastern steppe was Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek Khanate; the Kazakhs split from it c. 1465.
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Corrected (AP review): Samarkand and Bukhara were Timurid, not part of Moghulistan.
Java was not Malay sultanates: Majapahit ruled East Java, Madura and Bali until about 1527, and the Hindu Sunda Kingdom West Java until 1579.
The Wattasids and the Zayyanids were sultans, not caliphs.
The Hän people of the Yukon were coloured as the Ming Empire.
